translation: Target is defined as the proposition (with no hypotheses) asserting the conjunction of four statements concerning Peano arithmetic (PA), its standard consistency sentence PA.consistent.val (the arithmetic sentence ¬Prov_PA(⌜⊥⌝) built from PA's Δ₁ presentation), and the set of theorems (PA ∪ PA.Con).theory (the set of all arithmetic sentences derivable in classical first-order logic from PA together with the singleton set PA.Con = {PA.consistent.val}): (1) there exists a recursively enumerable set of arithmetic sentences F such that (PA ∪ PA.Con).theory equals F.theory (the set of all theorems of F); (2) for every arithmetic sentence σ in (PA ∪ PA.Con).theory, σ is true in the standard model ℕ; (3) PA.consistent.val belongs to (PA ∪ PA.Con).theory (i.e., is derivable from PA ∪ PA.Con); and (4) PA.consistent.val does not belong to PA.theory (i.e., is not derivable from PA).

divergences.description: TARGET hardcodes the first machine to the single concrete theory Peano Arithmetic (PA) rather than universally quantifying over an arbitrary sound, recursively enumerable formal system F (strong enough for Gödel's theorem). Both [P-L116] ('their first machine') and [P-C1] ('some sound formal system F'), as well as the author's claim, concern a general construction for any such machine; proving only the single PA instance is a major weakening that establishes an example rather than the general 'second machine' reply.

TARGET adds the consistency sentence PA.consistent.val (¬Prov_PA(⌜⊥⌝)) rather than a Gödel sentence or an arbitrary true unprovable formula, whereas [P-L116] speaks of 'a formula their first machine cannot produce as being true' and a 'Gödelian formula'. Since Con(PA) and the standard Gödel sentence of PA are provably equivalent in PA (yielding the same enlarged theorem set) and [P-C1] also discusses unprovability of consistency, this is a minor divergence.

TARGET omits the second half of [P-L116]—Lucas's counter-move that 'the second machine will have a Gödelian formula all of its own'—and stops after asserting that (PA ∪ PA.Con).theory is r.e.-axiomatizable, sound, and proves Con(PA) while PA does not. Because the author's claim explicitly scopes to the 'second machine' reply itself rather than Lucas's rebuttal, this omission is minor.

TARGET idealizes a 'machine' (or formal system) as the deductive closure of a recursively enumerable set of first-order arithmetic sentences in ℒₒᵣ (Def6), and idealizes 'soundness' as truth of all theorems in the standard model ℕ (Def3).

TARGET does not capture the epistemic claims of [P-C1] (whether human reasoning powers are captured by a sound formal system F, our inability to 'see' that F is consistent, and why Lucas's argument founders)—which are not expressible in the formal arithmetic framework—nor [P-C1]'s clause (b) that F proves 'Con(F) → G(F)'.

judgement.summary: TARGET is divergent because it specializes the 'second machine' construction to the single concrete theory PA rather than quantifying over an arbitrary sound, recursively enumerable first machine, thus establishing only one example instead of the general reply. It also exhibits minor idealizations and omissions, including using Con(PA) rather than a Gödel sentence, omitting Lucas's follow-up that the second machine has its own Gödelian formula, and not capturing the epistemic content of Chalmers's passage.
